disposition: No concrete source blocker found for the fixed96-input diagnostic. Proportionate rule/positive/negative/optional-variant review; not a claim of separately printed attestations for every generated paradigm.

primary_sources.finding: Kashika assigns at augmentation and pit to Lot first-person endings. Nyasa explicitly assigns pit to the ending rather than the augment, blocks ngit status, and permits guna. Balamanorama specifically discusses dual/plural vas/mas and stavava.

Apit sarvadhatuka endings behave as ngit; this is the ordinary weak-stem condition overridden by first-person imperative pit. The condition is term-specific, not a prohibition on every1.2.4 step elsewhere in the path.
Nasal infix a and as lose a before k/ngit sarvadhatuka; the same rule cannot delete the strong infix before the relevant pit imperative ending.

Deletion of final A of sna and reduplicated bases is restricted to k/ngit sarvadhatuka. Together with6.4.113 this explains imperative A retention, including where at changes the following initial vowel.
Sna/reduplicated A changes to I before consonantal k/ngit sarvadhatuka, excluding ghu. Direct mimavahai/mimamahai versus mimivahe/mimimahe controls corroborate the same first-person contrast.
Guna applies to final ik of a stem before sarvadhatuka/ardhadhatuka subject to blockers. Here the pit override permits the relevant strengthening in vowel-final athematic stems/suffixes.
Short penultimate ik has the corresponding guna rule; lih/rud are selected ordinary athematic examples, not causatives or inherited final-a Curadi probes.
Rudhadi uses snam; LSK gives weak rundhvah/rundhmah and strong runadhava/runadhama imperative forms.
The named stumbh/skumbh group licenses both sna and snu. Both resulting gold branches must remain accepted; no hidden branch is selected.
Optional loss of unconjoined suffix-u before m/v supplies valid weak-form variants; the full union is retained where applicable.

optional_variants: All96 prompts leave pada unspecified and accept the complete engine union. Independent review regenerated each task with explicit P/A separately and confirmed exact union equality. Stumbh/skumbh retain sna and snu alternatives.
novelty: Three related grammatical interactions, not a new ruleID: permissible guna, retained nasal-infix a, and retained sna/reduplicated A under3.4.92. Target/control inputs differ only in lakara; no extra per-question dimensions.
semantic_scope: Kartari dictionary entries need no chosen object/transitivity screen. Current shared21 entry/oracle exclusions plus the existing local uncertainties apply. No dialect toggle, prefixes or added sanadi.
limits: Every target is first-person non-singular imperative. Gana, voice and person distributions do not represent a final broad benchmark. Source licensing establishes validity, not hardness.
